title: Nyaya retrieval test query set
description:
Hand-verified Bangla/English test queries with gold labels.

MUST be built BEFORE Stage 1 (multi-query expansion) is built — the
multi_aspect and historical flags have no meaning without gold labels to
check them against. Every stage is measured against this set; the eval
harness ablation table is meaningless without it.

Principle: inflate the VERIFICATION, not the count. A small, fully
hand-verified set (15-30 queries covering all 7 categories) is worth more
than a padded set of LLM-generated filler. Every query below must be checked
against the actual docs/ corpus by a human before it enters the set.

Storage: eval/test_queries.json, versioned in git, SEPARATE from run-artifact
dirs (ingestion_output/, retrieval_traces/). This is code/config territory, not
generated output.

Categories (from RETRIEVAL_PIPELINE.md + the eval harness spec):
  1. single_provision_lookup  — answer is one known clause; gold section_number
  2. table_numeric_lookup      — wage figures, overtime rates, min wages;
                                  number/entity preservation is the top eval metric
  3. register_gap              — colloquial Bangla that doesn't share words with
                                  formal legal English; the query multi-query expansion
                                  exists to serve; core ablation row
  4. multi_aspect vs single_aspect_control  — paired queries; one genuinely two
                                  aspects (multi_aspect flag + MMR test), one the same
                                  stripped to one aspect (control)
  5. historical                — about law over time; historical flag + filter-swap test
  6. dual_layer_overlay_conflict — base vs 2025 Ordinance cover same provision;
                                  Stage 7 must surface both with labels
  7. advocacy_vs_primary_law   — CPD proposed wage vs actual gazette wage; must
                                  not present CPD's proposed figure as operative

query_id.description: Stable id matching the trace query_id (e.g. q0001). Traces and gold labels are joined by this.

query_bangla.description: The query in Bangla (the live path's input language). Typed/clean text — no ASR noise yet.

query_english.description: English equivalent where the register gap matters (for the register-gap category and for eval readability). Null where Bangla-only is fine.

gold_section_number.description: Gold section number where the answer is a specific provision (e.g. '23' or '23(3)'). Null where the answer is not a single provision (e.g. a table lookup or a multi-aspect query).

gold_answer_gist.description: Hand-written gist of the correct answer, for eval faithfulness / answer-correctness comparison. Not necessarily the full answer — enough to check whether the pipeline's answer is on the right track.

gold_source_doc.description: Which doc/ file the gold answer comes from (e.g. 'bangladesh_labour_act_2006_english_upto_2018'). For table_numeric and advocacy_vs_primary_law especially — to check the right source wins.

gold_figure.description: For table_numeric_lookup: the exact figure(s) the answer must preserve (wage amount, rate, date). Number/entity preservation is the single most important eval metric for this corpus — this field is the check.

multi_aspect_expected.description: Whether this query is EXPECTED to be flagged multi_aspect by Stage 1. Used to check Stage 1 flag correctness (the eval item: how often the flag fires and whether correctly).

historical_expected.description: Whether this query is EXPECTED to be flagged historical by Stage 1. Used to check the filter-swap behavior (Stage 2) and that superseded text surfaces only for historical queries.

dual_layer_expected.description: Whether this query is EXPECTED to surface a base+overlay dual_layer pair (Stage 7). Used to check conflict-handling correctness directly from the trace.

notes.description: Anything worth recording: which provision the query targets, why the category is what it is, known corpus quirks (e.g. a section that spans the 2018/2025 boundary), verification status.

verified_by.description: Who verified this query against the corpus (human). The set is hand-verified — this field records that it was, and by whom.

verified_date.description: When it was verified against the corpus.
